summary: Piscataquis County, ME tower built 1916 for the Maine Forestry District; still standing per FFLA, with a new recreational cab installed in 2020.

facts.design: Steel tower structure; 2020 replacement cab modeled on the Deboullie Mountain cab, designed by Kleinschmidt Associates

access.note: Bangor Daily News (Nov 2020) says hikers can visit the cab for recreation; no closure notice found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Trail or road to the site not described in the pages read

facts.agency: Maine Forestry District (historical); Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands (2020 cab work)

events.note: Lookout station built per the 1916 Forest Commissioner's report, with a watchman's camp at the foot; the 1919 report calls it a log tower built in 1916
July 1924 newspaper item says a 27-foot tower will be erected; completion not confirmed in the pages read

Allagash was among the last Maine towers closed; the article ties the final closures to a 1991 budget crisis. The year this tower closed was not found, so 1991 is the crisis year, not a confirmed closing date

Bureau of Parks and Lands had recently installed a new cab (Nov 2020 article); staff and volunteers stabilized the steel structure and a helicopter lifted the cab on. Exact August install date not verified

corrections.proposed: remove; no current height in the sources read
corrections.why: 6.1 m equals the 20-foot wooden tower in the 1920 inventory. A 1924 newspaper item planned a 27-foot tower instead, and no source read gives the height of the current steel structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 6.1 m (20 ft) matches the 1920 wooden tower; the 1924 plan was for 27 ft. No current height found, so height is left out of facts.

notes_for_editor: Brief events 2007 and 2008 (Morneault volunteer restoration) are NOT in this JSON: no page read supports them. A search result points to firelookout.org cr-me-2008.pdf (Maine Chapter Report 2008), which was not read because the page-read budget ran out; check it before adding those events. The brief's 'airlifted in August 2020' and 'one of three cabs replaced that week' are not confirmed: the BDN article says only 'recently installed', and the 2020 year-end report says 'reviewed in 2020'. Only the first 3,000 of about 6,200 characters of the BDN page were read, so cost and funding details were not used. Staffing 'not staffed' is an inference from the 'closed' note and the article's past-tense description of observers; treat it as medium confidence. The brief's status 'standing' is supported by the FFLA list and the 2020 article.
